sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know reported questions with a question word from A2 Unit 14 (*Preguntó dónde trabajó*) and *preguntar si* for yes/no questions from B1 Unit 33 (*Me preguntó si tenía tiempo*). Both lose the question marks, and the verb moves back one step, as in any report. This lesson puts the two kinds together and shows where else the same pattern appears.

sections.title: Question → reported question
rows: Me preguntó si había llegado el informe.
Me preguntó por qué me había ido.

sections.title: Three things to watch
sections.content:
• **Yes/no question → *si*.** *Si* has no accent. The question word of an information question stays, with its accent: *dónde*, *cuándo*, *por qué*, *quién*.
• **The verb moves back as in any report:** *saldrán* → *saldrían*, *vives* → *vivía*, *llegó* and *ha llamado* → *había llegado*, *había llamado*.
• **No question marks and no extra *que*.** Say *Me preguntó si venía*, not *Me preguntó que venía*: that would report a statement.
• **The person follows the point of view.** What she asked you (*¿Dónde vives?*) you retell as *Me preguntó dónde vivía*.

sections.title: Not only after *preguntar*
sections.content: The same pattern appears after verbs that are not about asking, when someone wonders or does not know: *Luis se preguntaba si Ana había llegado*, *No sabía dónde estaba su hermana*, *Nadie entendía por qué se había ido*. Nobody asked these questions out loud, but the question word, the accent and the verb shift work exactly as before. *Preguntarse* means "to wonder" (literally "to ask yourself").

items.english: She asked me if I had eaten.
He wanted to know when they would leave.

items.spanish: Luis se preguntaba si Ana había recibido su mensaje.
items.english: Luis was wondering whether Ana had received his message.

items.spanish: No sabía dónde estaban las llaves.
items.english: He did not know where the keys were.

sections.content: Find the clue in the original question: *si* for yes/no, the question word for information. It comes straight after the reporting verb, with no *que*.
